vulnerability.name: GHSA-jmr9-qjv8-65gv
vulnerability.description: extract-zip does not validate symlink targets when extracting zip archives, so an archive containing a relative symlink can point outside the extraction directory.

statements.impact_statement: The advisory's vulnerable range is `<= 2.0.1` and 2.0.1 is the highest version ever published, so no upgrade or override target exists; GitHub reports first_patched: NONE. extract-zip reaches this repository through exactly one path — @puppeteer/browsers <- puppeteer-core <- lighthouse <- @lhci/cli, a devDependency of apps/docs used only by the `test:budget` gate — and that path never calls it. Measured 2026-08-18: none of the three packages carries an install script, so `pnpm install` never invokes it; `test:budget` ran green under a module-load probe over its 17 node processes with zero loads of extract-zip, @puppeteer/browsers, or yauzl, the probe having been positive-controlled against a forced require first; the isolation does not rest on the CHROME_PATH that hands Lighthouse a Playwright Chromium, because with it unset lhci fails `Chrome installation not found` rather than falling back to a browser download; and the published `memhtml` package declares 12 dependencies, none of them on this path, because apps/docs is not among the packages feeding that manifest. Revisit if the docs toolchain ever downloads its own browser instead of being handed one — that, not a fixed release, is what would make this reachable.
